metadata.source: SAMHSA, NIMH, American Psychological Association, CDC, Mayo Clinic, Cleveland Clinic, FDA, TED Talks
metadata.description: Evidence-based mental health treatments for youth - expanded with 14 additional modalities
metadata.note: Effectiveness percentages based on clinical trials, meta-analyses, and peer-reviewed research
metadata.phases: Original 15 treatments + Phase 2: 10 new evidence-based modalities + Phase 3: 4 emerging treatments (2025-2026)

treatments.name: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)
treatments.description: Evidence-based talk therapy focusing on changing negative thought patterns and behaviors. Highly effective for youth.
treatments.considerations: Requires motivated participant; may take 8-12 weeks to see full benefits

treatments.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
treatments.description: Specialized therapy combining CBT with mindfulness and acceptance strategies. Excellent for self-harm and emotional regulation.
treatments.considerations: More intensive; requires 1-2 years commitment; best for moderate-severe cases

treatments.name: Family-Based Treatment (FBT)
treatments.description: Involves parents/guardians in treatment to improve family dynamics and support systems. Highly effective for younger youth.
treatments.considerations: Requires family involvement; may reveal family conflicts

treatments.name: Interpersonal Therapy (IPT)
treatments.description: Focuses on improving interpersonal relationships and addressing social isolation. Particularly effective for depression.
treatments.considerations: Best for depression with social component; requires some social engagement capacity

treatments.name: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)
treatments.description: Antidepressant medications that increase serotonin. First-line medication for depression and anxiety in youth.
treatments.duration: 4-8 weeks to feel effects; 6-12 months typical
treatments.considerations: Requires medical supervision; side effects possible; take 4-8 weeks for full effect

treatments.name: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT)
treatments.description: Combines mindfulness meditation with cognitive therapy to prevent relapse, especially in depression. 8-week program.
treatments.considerations: Group format; requires consistency; works better as maintenance after other treatment

treatments.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
treatments.description: Teaches psychological flexibility by accepting thoughts/feelings while pursuing values-aligned living.
treatments.considerations: Better for motivated teens; requires willingness to feel discomfort; metaphor-based

treatments.name: Behavioral Activation
treatments.description: Systematic scheduling of meaningful activities to counteract depression-related withdrawal. Practical, self-directed.
treatments.considerations: Requires some motivation to start; very accessible; works best as part of broader treatment

treatments.name: Exposure & Response Prevention (ERP)
treatments.description: Gold-standard anxiety treatment: gradual exposure to feared situations without engaging in compulsions.
treatments.considerations: Requires skilled therapist; involves intentional anxiety; demands courage; very effective when done well

treatments.name: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I)
treatments.description: Sleep restriction, stimulus control, and cognitive restructuring for insomnia. Critical for teen sleep deprivation epidemic.
treatments.duration: 4-6 sessions; can be self-directed with app
treatments.considerations: Requires 4-6 weeks for full benefit; initial sleep restriction can be uncomfortable; highly effective

treatments.name: Problem-Solving Therapy (PST)
treatments.description: Teaches structured approach to define problems, generate solutions, evaluate, implement, and learn.
treatments.considerations: Requires willingness to try solutions; empowering for teens; teachable in schools

treatments.name: Emotion Regulation Skills (DBT Modules)
treatments.description: Standalone DBT skills (not full therapy): mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion regulation, interpersonal. Teachable in groups.
treatments.considerations: Skills-based (not therapy); requires practice; works well as school program; best as maintenance

treatments.name: Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy (VRET)
treatments.description: FDA-cleared VR environments for anxiety exposure. 95% youth engagement. Emerging gold standard for tech-native youth.
treatments.considerations: Emerging technology; requires VR equipment and trained therapist; cost $100-300/session; growing insurance coverage

treatments.name: Social Connection & Community Interventions
treatments.description: Addressing loneliness epidemic through quality connections. Highly preventive. 60%+ youth report chronic loneliness.
treatments.considerations: Requires bravery for socially anxious; loneliness = 2.5x depression risk; foundational for wellbeing

treatments.name: Crisis Intervention & Safety Planning
treatments.description: Crisis lines, safety plans, and emergency interventions for acute mental health crises. Essential for severe cases.
treatments.considerations: For emergencies only; not substitute for ongoing treatment; follow-up care essential

treatments.name: Movement & Somatic Therapy
treatments.description: Body-based processing through dance, movement, and somatic awareness. Releases stored trauma and tension.
treatments.considerations: Requires comfort with movement; group formats highly beneficial; accessible through studios and schools

treatments.name: Arts & Expressive Therapies
treatments.description: Non-verbal processing through art, music, drama, or writing. Powerful for emotional expression and trauma.
treatments.considerations: No artistic skill required; community formats highly beneficial; available in schools and centers

treatments.name: Positive Psychology Interventions
treatments.description: Gratitude, strengths, and savoring practices. Evidence-based happiness practices that rewire negativity bias.
treatments.duration: 5-10 min daily; 2-3 weeks to notice shift
treatments.considerations: Best as maintenance or prevention; works well with other therapies; highly self-directed

treatments.name: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) - Youth Adapted
treatments.description: 8-week program (6 weeks for youth) with body scans, breathing, yoga, and mindful daily activities.
treatments.considerations: Group format; requires consistency; works well in schools; builds over 6-8 weeks

treatments.name: Schema Therapy
treatments.description: Identifies core patterns from childhood and uses imagery to build 'healthy adult' responses. For complex/chronic cases.
treatments.considerations: Complex work; requires skilled therapist; best for adults 18+; deeper personal exploration needed

treatments.name: Interpersonal Effectiveness Skills (DBT)
treatments.description: DBT skill module: DEAR MAN, GIVE, FAST strategies for communication, relationships, and boundaries.
treatments.considerations: Skills-based; requires practice in real situations; works well with groups or schools

treatments.name: Worry Time Container
treatments.description: Set aside 10-15 min to worry deliberately, then consciously put worries aside. Teaches control over rumination.
treatments.considerations: Simple but effective; works best with other anxiety interventions; highly accessible

treatments.name: Visualization & Guided Imagery
treatments.description: Guided visualization to safe place or desired outcomes. Calms nervous system and reduces anxiety.
treatments.considerations: Works well with apps; requires quiet space; very accessible; complements other treatments

treatments.name: Peer Support & Support Groups
treatments.description: Structured peer support groups or trained peer mentors. Reduces isolation and normalizes struggle.
treatments.considerations: Requires vulnerability; group dynamics matter; online options available; highly accessible

treatments.name: Lifestyle Interventions (Sleep, Exercise, Nutrition)
treatments.description: Evidence-based lifestyle: 8+ hours sleep, 30+ min exercise, balanced nutrition. Foundation for all mental health.
treatments.considerations: Often neglected; must combine with other treatments; habit-building takes 21-30 days

treatments.name: Academic Pressure & Perfectionism Coaching
treatments.description: Specialized coaching combining ACT, behavioral strategies, and values clarification for perfectionism and academic stress. Increasingly needed: teens report rising academic pressure and performance anxiety.
treatments.considerations: Emerging concern in 2025-2026; integrates ACT principles; highly relevant to achievement-oriented teens

treatments.name: Digital Wellness & Screen Time Management
treatments.description: Structured approach to healthy digital boundaries, recognizing social media as both tool and stressor. Addresses emerging digital addiction and AI-related anxiety.
treatments.considerations: New category in 2025; family involvement helpful; requires practical boundary-setting; growing research base

treatments.name: Loneliness & Social Connection Building
treatments.description: Targeted intervention for epidemic-scale loneliness: peer connection programs, school connectedness, quality relationships over quantity. Lacking social connection doubles depression risk.
treatments.considerations: Critical emerging need; social anxiety may require support; quality over quantity matters; sustainable through community

treatments.name: Cost-Free & Accessible Mental Health Resources
treatments.description: Comprehensive guide to free/low-cost mental health: crisis lines (988), peer support (7 Cups), apps (CBT-i Coach), hotlines, teletherapy sliding scales, school resources.
treatments.considerations: Addresses critical resource gap identified by teens; equity issue; complements professional care
